sources: Türkiye Maarif Vakfı, Türkçenin Yabancı Dil Olarak Öğretimi Programı — section 7, 'Seviyelere Göre Dil Yapıları Listesi' (pp. 79-81). PDF: https://kutuphane.turkiyemaarif.org/uploads/Turkcenin_Yabanci_Dil_Olarak_Ogretimi_Programi1-q2nrq.pdf (read in full). This is the CEFR-based official programme and the only source reached that gives an explicit A1-C1 grammar list.

Erdil, M. & Açık, F. (2021). 'Türkiye Maarif Vakfı Türkçenin Yabancı Dil Olarak Öğretimi Programı ile Türkçe Öğretim Setlerinde Dil Bilgisi İçeriklerinin İncelenmesi', International Journal of Languages' Education and Teaching 9(4), 130-158. https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/3699834 (read in full). Tables 1-7 reproduce, level by level, the grammar syllabus of: Yunus Emre Enstitüsü Yedi İklim Türkçe; Yeni Hitit (Ankara Üniversitesi TÖMER); Gazi Üniversitesi Yabancılar İçin Türkçe Dil Bilgisi; İstanbul Yabancılar İçin Türkçe. Used as the proxy for the YEE and TÖMER syllabi, whose own PDFs are not public.

MEB Hayat Boyu Öğrenme Genel Müdürlüğü (2017). Yabancı Diller Türkçe A1 Seviyesi Kurs Programı. https://ookgm.meb.gov.tr/meb_iys_dosyalar/2021_01/05115713_YabancY_Diller_YabancY_Diller_Turkce__A1_Seviyesi.pdf (read in full). Theme/can-do based, not a grammar list; used only to check which structures surface in A1 example language.

Diller İçin Avrupa Ortak Başvuru Metni (the Turkish CEFR adaptation) — consulted conceptually only. Like the CEFR itself it gives level descriptors, not a grammar inventory, so it contributes no topic here; see tr-report.md.

a1.name: Turkish alphabet and the ı / i pair
a1.note: The Turkish alphabet has 29 letters and is close to one-letter-one-sound. Dotless ı and dotted i are two different letters (capitals I and İ), and the difference decides which vowel a suffix takes.
a1.test: The sentence contains at least one word spelled with ı and at least one word spelled with i, so the two letters are contrasted in the same sentence.

a1.name: Vowel harmony, two-fold suffixes (A → a / e)
a1.note: Suffixes written with A have two shapes: -a after a back vowel (a, ı, o, u), -e after a front vowel (e, i, ö, ü). The plural -lAr, the dative -A and the locative/ablative vowels all work this way.
a1.test: The sentence contains at least two words carrying the same two-fold suffix (e.g. -lAr, -A, -DA, -DAn) in both of its shapes, one after a back-vowel stem and one after a front-vowel stem.

a1.name: Vowel harmony, four-fold suffixes (I → ı / i / u / ü)
a1.note: Suffixes written with I have four shapes. The vowel copies the frontness and the rounding of the stem's last vowel: a/ı→ı, e/i→i, o/u→u, ö/ü→ü. The accusative -I, the genitive -In, the possessives and the copular endings are all four-fold.
a1.example: Onun gözü mavi, benim kitabım eski.
a1.test: The sentence contains at least one four-fold suffix (accusative -I, genitive -In, possessive -Im/-In/-(s)I, copular -(y)Im) whose vowel is ı, i, u or ü as required by the stem's last vowel.

a1.name: Consonant assimilation (ünsüz benzeşmesi): D → t, C → ç
a1.note: After a voiceless consonant (p, ç, t, k, f, h, s, ş) a suffix beginning with d hardens to t and one beginning with c hardens to ç: -DA → -ta/-te, -DAn → -tan/-ten, -DI → -tı/-ti.
a1.test: The sentence contains a suffix of the D-class (-DA, -DAn, -DI, -DIk) written with t because the stem ends in a voiceless consonant — e.g. markette, kitaptan, çıktı.

a1.name: Consonant softening (ünsüz yumuşaması): p, ç, t, k → b, c, d, ğ
a1.note: A stem-final p, ç, t or k becomes b, c, d or ğ when a vowel-initial suffix follows: kitap → kitabı, ağaç → ağacı, git- → gidiyor, ekmek → ekmeği. Learners must spell the changed stem, not the dictionary form.
a1.test: The sentence contains a word whose stem-final p/ç/t/k is written as b/c/d/ğ before a vowel-initial suffix (kitabı, ağacı, gideceğim, ekmeği).

a1.name: Verb-final word order and dropped subject pronouns
a1.note: The finite verb or predicate comes last; modifiers precede what they modify. Because the predicate carries a person ending, the subject pronoun is normally left out.
a1.test: The last word of the sentence is the finite predicate (a verb, or a noun/adjective with a copular ending, var/yok, or değil).

a1.name: Plural suffix -lAr
a1.note: Plural is marked by -lar/-ler. A plural non-human subject normally takes a singular verb, and a noun after a numeral stays singular.
a1.test: The sentence contains a noun ending in -lar or -ler used as a plural.

a1.name: Numerals and the singular noun after them
a1.note: Cardinal numbers precede the noun and the noun stays singular: iki kitap, not iki kitaplar. 'bir' also does duty as the indefinite article.
a1.test: The sentence contains a numeral (or bir) directly before a noun, and that noun carries no -lAr.

a1.name: Demonstratives bu / şu / o and burası / şurası / orası
a1.note: Three-way distance: bu (here), şu (there, just pointed at), o (yonder / already known). The place forms burası, şurası, orası are used as nouns.
a1.example: Bu kitap yeni, şu masa eski.
a1.test: The sentence contains bu, şu or o used as a demonstrative before a noun, or burası/şurası/orası used as a place noun.

a1.name: Personal pronouns ben, sen, o, biz, siz, onlar
a1.note: One set of pronouns for all genders: o is he, she and it. siz is both plural and polite. The pronoun is used mainly for contrast, since the ending already marks person.
a1.test: The sentence contains at least one of ben, sen, o, biz, siz, onlar used as a pronoun.

a1.name: Copular endings (ek fiil geniş zaman) — no separate verb 'to be'
a1.note: There is no verb 'to be'. Person is suffixed straight onto the noun or adjective: -(y)Im, -sIn, -(dIr), -(y)Iz, -sInIz, -(lAr). The third person usually has no ending at all.
a1.test: The predicate is a noun or adjective carrying a copular person ending (-(y)Im, -sIn, -(y)Iz, -sInIz, -DIr), or a bare third-person nominal predicate.

a1.name: Nominal negation with değil
a1.note: Nouns and adjectives are negated by the separate word değil after the predicate, never by the verbal -mA. değil itself takes the person ending: değilim, değilsin.
a1.test: The sentence contains değil as a separate word after a noun or adjective predicate.

a1.name: Question particle mI as a separate word
a1.note: Yes/no questions add mı / mi / mu / mü, written as a separate word after the questioned element but harmonising with it. Person endings attach to the particle: geliyor musun, öğrenci misin.
a1.test: The sentence contains mı, mi, mu or mü written as a separate word (optionally with a person ending attached to it, e.g. misin, musunuz), and its vowel harmonises with the preceding word.

a1.name: Existence and possession: var / yok
a1.note: There is no verb 'to have'. Existence is var (there is) and yok (there is not); possession is expressed as possessor + possessed with a possessive suffix + var/yok: Benim arabam var.
a1.example: Evde su var ama ekmek yok.
a1.test: The sentence ends in var or yok as the predicate.

a1.name: Locative case -DA (in / on / at)
a1.note: -da / -de / -ta / -te marks location and, with var/yok, the place where something is. Also used for times: saat üçte.
a1.test: The sentence contains a noun ending in -da, -de, -ta or -te expressing location or time.

a1.name: Adjectives before the noun, with no agreement
a1.note: An adjective stands directly before its noun and never changes for number or case: büyük ev, büyük evler, büyük evde.
a1.test: The sentence contains an adjective immediately before a noun, carrying no suffix of its own.

a1.name: Possessive suffixes -Im, -In, -(s)I, -ImIz, -InIz, -lArI
a1.note: The owner is marked on the thing owned: ev → evim (my house), evin, evi, evimiz, eviniz, evleri. After a vowel the third person adds the buffer s: araba → arabası.
a1.example: Benim evim küçük, senin evin büyük.
a1.test: The sentence contains a noun carrying a possessive suffix (-Im, -In, -(s)I, -ImIz, -InIz, -lArI).

a1.name: Genitive -(n)In and the possessive construction (isim tamlaması)
a1.note: A possessor takes the genitive -(n)In and the possessed takes the third-person possessive: çocuğun kitabı. When the first noun is generic the genitive is dropped: okul kitabı (a schoolbook).
a1.test: The sentence contains a two-noun phrase in which the second noun carries -(s)I/-lArI, with the first noun either in the genitive (-(n)In) or bare in the generic type.

a1.name: The buffer n before a case suffix (zamir n'si)
a1.note: After a third-person possessive, or after bu/şu/o, an n appears before any case ending: evi → evinde, bu → bunda, onu → onunla. Learners regularly leave it out.
a1.test: The sentence contains a word in which n stands between a third-person possessive (or bu/şu/o) and a case suffix — evinde, evinden, bunda, onunla.

a1.name: Dative case -(y)A (to / towards)
a1.note: -a / -e marks the goal of motion and the indirect object; after a vowel the buffer y appears: okula, eve, arabaya. Many verbs govern it: gitmek, gelmek, bakmak, başlamak.
a1.test: The sentence contains a noun ending in -a, -e, -ya or -ye expressing a goal or an indirect object.

a1.name: Ablative case -DAn (from / out of)
a1.note: -dan / -den / -tan / -ten marks the source, the starting point, and the standard in comparison.
a1.test: The sentence contains a noun ending in -dan, -den, -tan or -ten expressing a source or starting point.

a1.name: Accusative case -(y)I, only on definite objects
a1.note: A direct object takes -ı/-i/-u/-ü only when it is definite or specific: Kitabı okuyorum (the book) against Kitap okuyorum (I read books). Turkish makes a split here that English does not.
a1.test: The sentence contains a direct object carrying -ı, -i, -u, -ü (or -yı/-yi/-yu/-yü after a vowel), and that object is definite.

a1.name: Present continuous -Iyor and vowel narrowing
a1.note: -ıyor / -iyor / -uyor / -üyor covers what is happening now and, in beginner Turkish, what happens habitually. A stem-final a or e narrows before it: başla- → başlıyor, ye- → yiyor.
a1.test: The sentence contains a finite verb ending in -ıyor/-iyor/-uyor/-üyor plus a person ending.

a1.name: Verbal negation -mA
a1.note: Verbs are negated by -ma/-me placed between the stem and the tense suffix: gitmedim, gitmiyorum, gitmeyeceğim. Note the narrowing in gitmiyorum.
a1.test: The sentence contains a finite verb with -ma/-me (or its narrowed -mı-/-mi-/-mu-/-mü- before -yor) between the stem and the tense suffix.

a1.name: Infinitive -mAk and -mAk istemek
a1.note: -mak/-mek is the dictionary form and the complement of verbs like istemek and sevmek: Su içmek istiyorum. With sevmek it usually appears as -mAyI: yüzmeyi sevmek.
a1.test: The sentence contains a verb in -mak/-mek serving as the complement of another verb (istemek, sevmek, başlamak…).

a1.name: Imperative
a1.note: The bare stem is the singular imperative (gel!, aç!); -(y)In / -(y)InIz is the plural and polite form (gelin, geliniz). Negative: gelme, gelmeyin.
a1.test: The predicate is a bare verb stem, or a verb with -(y)In/-(y)InIz, used as a command.

a1.name: Witnessed past -DI
a1.note: -dı / -di / -du / -dü (-tı/-ti/-tu/-tü after a voiceless consonant) reports something the speaker saw, did or knows first hand. Person endings: geldim, geldin, geldi, geldik.
a1.test: The sentence contains a finite verb in -DI plus a person ending (geldim, gitti, okuduk), used for an event the speaker vouches for.

a1.name: Past copula -(y)DI on nouns and adjectives
a1.note: The past of a nominal predicate is -(y)dı/-(y)di/-(y)du/-(y)dü plus a person ending: hastaydım, evdeydi, öğrenciydik. There is still no verb 'to be'.
a1.test: The predicate is a noun or adjective carrying -(y)DI plus a person ending (mutluydum, evdeydi, öğrenciydik).

a1.name: Future -(y)AcAk
a1.note: -acak / -ecek marks the future. The k softens to ğ before the first-person endings: gideceğim, geleceğiz.
a1.test: The sentence contains a finite verb in -acak/-ecek (or -eceğ-/-acağ- before a vowel) plus a person ending.

a1.name: -DAn önce / -DAn sonra
a1.note: önce (before) and sonra (after) follow a noun in the ablative: dersten sonra, yemekten önce.
a1.test: The sentence contains a noun in the ablative (-DAn) immediately followed by önce or sonra.

a1.name: ile / -(y)lA — 'with' and 'and'
a1.note: ile joins two nouns and also means 'with, by means of'. It is usually written as the suffix -(y)la/-(y)le: arkadaşımla, otobüsle. With pronouns the genitive is used: benimle.
a1.test: The sentence contains ile as a separate word or -la/-le/-yla/-yle suffixed to a noun or pronoun.

a1.name: Derivation -lI (with) and -sIz (without)
a1.note: -lı/-li/-lu/-lü makes 'having X' and also 'from place X' (Ankaralı); -sız/-siz/-suz/-süz makes 'without X'.
a1.example: Sütlü kahve içiyorum, sütsüz çay istemiyorum.
a1.test: The sentence contains a word formed with -lI or -sIz from a noun.

a1.name: -DAki (the one in / on / at)
a1.note: -ki attached to a locative turns a place phrase into a modifier: masadaki kitap, evdeki telefon. It does not obey vowel harmony.
a1.test: The sentence contains a noun ending in -daki/-deki/-taki/-teki used to modify a following noun or standing alone as a pronoun.

a1.name: Comparison with -DAn daha and the superlative en
a1.note: The standard of comparison takes the ablative and daha is optional: Bu ev şu evden (daha) büyük. The superlative is en before the adjective: en güzel.
a1.example: Bu ev şu evden daha büyük.
a1.test: The sentence contains a noun in the ablative before an adjective (with or without daha), or the word en before an adjective.

a1.name: The clitic dA ('also, too'), written separately
a1.note: de / da meaning 'also, too' is a separate word and harmonises only for backness: Ben de geliyorum. It must not be confused with the locative suffix -DA, which is written joined: Bende para var.
a1.test: The sentence contains de or da standing as a separate word meaning 'also/too' (not a locative suffix attached to a noun).

a1.name: Basic conjunctions ve, ama, çünkü, veya
a1.note: The first sentence connectors: ve (and), ama (but), çünkü (because), veya (or). ve joins words and clauses; çünkü opens the reason clause after the main clause.
a1.test: The sentence contains ve, ama, çünkü or veya joining two words or two clauses.

a2.name: Reported / inferred past -mIş against witnessed -DI
a2.note: -mış / -miş / -muş / -müş reports something the speaker did not witness: hearsay, inference, or surprise at a result. It contrasts directly with -DI, which claims first-hand knowledge. Turkish forces this choice on every past-tense sentence.
a2.test: The sentence contains a finite verb in -mIş plus a person ending, used for an unwitnessed, reported or inferred event — ideally alongside or against a -DI form.

a2.name: Reported copula -(y)mIş on nouns and adjectives
a2.note: The nominal predicate gets the same evidential marking: hastaymış (apparently he was ill), öğretmenmiş. Formed with -(y)mIş plus the person ending.
a2.test: The predicate is a noun or adjective carrying -(y)mIş (hastaymış, evdeymiş, öğretmenmiş).

a2.name: Aorist -Ir against the present continuous -Iyor
a2.note: -r / -ır / -er / -ar states habits, general truths, willingness and offers: Her sabah çay içerim; Su 100 derecede kaynar; Yardım ederim. -Iyor reports what is going on now. The negative is irregular: -mAm, -mAzsIn, -mAz.
a2.test: The sentence contains a finite verb in the aorist (-r, -ar, -er, -ır/-ir/-ur/-ür) or its negative (-mAm, -mAz), used for a habit, a general truth or willingness rather than an event in progress.

a2.name: Ability and permission -(y)Abil, negative -(y)AmA
a2.note: -(y)abil- / -(y)ebil- inserted before the tense marks 'can, may': gelebilirim, gidebilir misin. The negative drops bil: gelemem, gidemedim.
a2.test: The sentence contains a verb with -(y)Abil- before its tense ending, or the negative -(y)AmA- form (gelemem, yapamadı).

a2.name: Necessity -mAlI and the zorunda / gerek / lazım set
a2.note: -malı / -meli marks obligation: gitmeliyim. Alternatives: -mAk zorundayım (I have to), -mAm gerek / lazım (I need to).
a2.test: The sentence contains a verb in -mAlI plus a person ending, or the pattern -mAk zorunda / -mAsI gerek / -mAsI lazım.

a2.name: Optative -(y)A, above all the 'let's' form -(y)AlIm
a2.note: -(y)ayım / -(y)alım makes suggestions: Gidelim (let's go), Ben bakayım (let me look). It is the ordinary way to propose something.
a2.test: The sentence contains a verb ending in -(y)AlIm or -(y)AyIm used as a suggestion.

a2.name: Converb -(y)ArAk (by doing, while doing)
a2.note: -arak / -erek says how the main action is carried out: Koşarak geldim (I came running). Both verbs share one subject.
a2.test: The sentence contains a non-finite verb in -arak/-erek modifying the main verb.

a2.name: Converb -(y)Ip (and then)
a2.note: -ıp / -ip / -up / -üp chains two actions of the same subject and lets the tense and person be stated only once, on the last verb: Eve gidip uyudum.
a2.test: The sentence contains a verb ending in -ıp/-ip/-up/-üp followed later by a finite verb sharing its subject.

a2.name: Converb -mAdAn (without doing)
a2.note: -madan / -meden means 'without doing': Kahvaltı yapmadan çıktım. Note that it is not itself a negative clause with a person ending.
a2.test: The sentence contains a non-finite verb ending in -madan/-meden meaning 'without doing'.

a2.name: -mAdAn önce and -DIktAn sonra
a2.note: These build time clauses: yemek yemeden önce (before eating), ders bittikten sonra (after the lesson ended). They replace the noun in the A1 -DAn önce / -DAn sonra pattern with a verb.
a2.test: The sentence contains a verb in -mAdAn immediately followed by önce, or a verb in -DIktAn immediately followed by sonra.

a2.name: Subject participle -(y)An
a2.note: -an / -en makes a relative clause whose head is the subject of the clause: burada çalışan adam (the man who works here). It does the work of English 'who / which' + verb.
a2.test: The sentence contains a verb in -an/-en modifying a following noun that is the subject of that verb.

a2.name: Verbal nouns -mA, -mAk, -(y)Iş
a2.note: Verbs become nouns with -ma/-me (the act), -mak/-mek (the infinitive) or -(y)ış/-(y)iş (the manner). They then take case and possessive endings: yüzmeyi seviyorum, gelişi hoşuma gitti.
a2.test: The sentence contains a verb nominalised with -mA, -mAk or -(y)Iş and carrying a case or possessive ending.

a2.name: Purpose: -mAk için, -mAsI için, -mAk üzere
a2.note: -mak için gives the purpose when both clauses share a subject; -mAsI için when the subjects differ: Ekmek almak için çıktım / Gelmesi için aradım.
a2.test: The sentence contains -mAk için or -mAsI için (or -mAk üzere) expressing purpose.

a2.name: gibi and kadar (like, as … as)
a2.note: gibi compares kind ('like'), kadar compares degree ('as … as'): buz gibi soğuk, benim kadar uzun. With pronouns they take the genitive: benim gibi.
a2.test: The sentence contains gibi or kadar as a postposition after a noun or pronoun.

a2.name: -CA and -A göre
a2.note: -ca / -ce makes an adverb or 'according to' ('bence' = in my opinion, 'kolayca' = easily); -A göre means 'according to, compared with': bana göre, ona göre.
a2.example: Bana göre bu film çok güzel.
a2.test: The sentence contains a word in -CA used adverbially, or a noun/pronoun in the dative followed by göre.

a2.name: Direct speech with demek and diye
a2.note: Quoted words are followed by dedi, or by diye plus a verb of speaking or asking: 'Nerelisin?' diye sordu. Turkish quotes directly far more than English does.
a2.test: The sentence contains quoted words followed by de- (dedi, diyor) or by diye plus a speech verb.

a2.name: Paired conjunctions hem…hem, ne…ne, ya…ya, ister…ister
a2.note: hem … hem (both … and), ya … ya (either … or), ister … ister (whether … or), and ne … ne (neither … nor), which — unlike English — keeps the verb positive: Ne çay ne kahve içerim.
a2.test: The sentence contains one of the paired sets hem…hem, ya…ya, ister…ister, ne…ne with both halves present.

a2.name: Reflexive kendi
a2.note: kendi means 'own' and, with possessive and case endings, 'myself, yourself…': kendi odam, kendimi, kendine. It also intensifies: Bunu kendim yaptım.
a2.test: The sentence contains kendi, alone or with a possessive/case ending (kendim, kendimi, kendine, kendi + noun).

a2.name: hiç, kimse, hiçbir with a negative verb
a2.note: Negative words need the verb to be negative as well: Hiç kimse gelmedi, Hiçbir şey söylemedim. A positive verb after them is wrong.
a2.test: The sentence contains hiç, kimse, hiçbir or hiçbir şey together with a verb carrying the negative -mA (or a değil / yok predicate).

a2.name: Reduplication (ikileme)
a2.note: Doubling a word makes an adverb or intensifies it: yavaş yavaş (slowly, bit by bit), tek tek, zaman zaman, ev ev. Very frequent in everyday Turkish.
a2.test: The sentence contains the same word written twice in a row as one adverbial expression.

a2.name: Converb -A … -A (doing and doing)
a2.note: The same verb doubled in -a/-e describes a manner going on throughout the main action: güle güle (laughing), koşa koşa (at a run).
a2.test: The sentence contains the same verb stem repeated twice with -a/-e (güle güle, koşa koşa, baka baka).

a2.name: Intensified adjectives (pekiştirme)
a2.note: Colours and some adjectives intensify by copying the first syllable plus m, p, r or s: masmavi, bembeyaz, kapkara, sımsıcak. The forms are fixed and must be learned.
a2.test: The sentence contains an intensified adjective of the masmavi / bembeyaz / kapkara / sımsıcak type.

a2.name: Result connectors bu yüzden, bu sebeple, onun için
a2.note: These open the result clause after the reason has been given, the mirror image of A1's çünkü: Hastaydım, bu yüzden gelmedim.
a2.test: The sentence contains bu yüzden, bu sebeple, bu nedenle or onun için introducing a result clause.

b1.name: Past continuous -Iyordu (şimdiki zamanın hikâyesi)
b1.note: -ıyordu / -iyordu sets the background of a past story: what was going on when something else happened. It is the first of the compound tenses.
b1.test: The sentence contains a finite verb in -Iyordu plus a person ending.

b1.name: Compound past tenses with -(y)DI: -mIştI, -AcAktI, -Irdı
b1.note: Any tense can be pushed into the past by adding -(y)DI: gelmişti (had come), gelecekti (was going to come), gelirdi (used to come). Turkish calls these hikâye birleşik zaman.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb carrying a tense suffix followed by -(y)DI — gitmişti, gelecekti, okurdu, gidiyordu.

b1.name: Compound reported tenses with -(y)mIş: -Iyormuş, -AcAkmIş, -Irmış
b1.note: The same stacking with -(y)mIş marks the whole statement as hearsay: geliyormuş (they say he is coming), gelecekmiş, gelirmiş. Turkish calls these rivayet birleşik zaman.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb carrying a tense suffix followed by -(y)mIş — gelecekmiş, geliyormuş, gelirmiş.

b1.name: Real conditional -(y)sA
b1.note: -sa / -se attached after a tense gives a real condition: Zamanın varsa gel; Yarın yağmur yağarsa gitmeyiz. The main clause usually stands in the aorist or the future.
b1.test: The sentence contains a subordinate clause whose verb or predicate ends in -sA / -(y)sA and a main clause depending on it.

b1.name: Conditional on each tense: -Iyorsa, -DIysA, -mIşsA, -AcAksA, -Irsa
b1.note: The condition marker is added after the tense, so the condition itself is anchored in time: geldiyse (if he came), geliyorsa, gelecekse.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb with a tense suffix followed by -(y)sA — geldiyse, geliyorsa, gelecekse, gelmişse.

b1.name: Wishes and unreal conditions: keşke … -sAydI
b1.note: -saydı / -seydi with keşke expresses a regret or an unreal condition: Keşke burada olsaydın. The main clause then takes -AcAktI or -Irdı.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb in -sAydI, usually after keşke or eğer.

b1.name: Converb -(y)IncA (when, as soon as)
b1.note: -ınca / -ince builds a time clause without a person ending; the subject is read from the possessive-free context: Eve gelince beni ara.
b1.test: The sentence contains a non-finite verb ending in -ınca/-ince/-unca/-ünce introducing a time clause.

b1.name: -(y)IncAyA kadar / -(y)AnA kadar (until)
b1.note: Marks the end point of the main action: Sen gelinceye kadar bekledim.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb in -(y)IncAyA or -(y)AnA followed by kadar (or dek / değin).

b1.name: -Ir … -mAz (as soon as)
b1.note: The same verb in the positive aorist and then the negative aorist means 'the moment that': Eve gelir gelmez uyudu.
b1.test: The sentence contains the same verb stem twice, first in the aorist and then in -mAz (gelir gelmez, görür görmez).

b1.name: -(y)ken (while, when)
b1.note: -(y)ken attaches to a tense or to a nominal to mean 'while': yemek yerken, çocukken, evdeyken. It never harmonises — it is always -ken.
b1.test: The sentence contains a word ending in -ken (yerken, gelirken, çocukken, evdeyken).

b1.name: -DIkçA (as, the more … the more)
b1.note: -dıkça / -dikçe expresses a proportion or a repeated condition: Onu gördükçe mutlu oluyorum; Yağmur yağdıkça hava soğudu.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb ending in -dıkça/-dikçe/-dukça/-dükçe (or -tıkça after a voiceless stem).

b1.name: -(y)AlI and -DIğIndAn beri (since)
b1.note: Both mark a starting point in time: Buraya geleli üç yıl oldu; Geldiğinden beri hiç aramadı.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb in -(y)AlI, or a verb in -DIğIndAn followed by beri.

b1.name: Object participle -DIk + possessive
b1.note: -dık / -dik plus a possessive suffix makes the relative clause whose head is not the subject: okuduğum kitap (the book I read), oturduğumuz ev. The possessive marks who did it.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb in -DIk carrying a possessive suffix and modifying a following noun (okuduğum kitap, gittiğin şehir).

b1.name: Future participle -(y)AcAk + possessive
b1.note: The same construction for events still to come: yarın gideceğim şehir, alacağımız ev.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb in -(y)AcAk carrying a possessive suffix and modifying a following noun.

b1.name: Reported statements: -DIğInI / -AcAğInI + verb of knowing or saying
b1.note: Turkish has no 'that' clause. The subordinate verb is nominalised and takes case: Geleceğini biliyorum (I know he will come); Hasta olduğunu duydum.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb in -DIğI or -(y)AcAğI carrying a possessive plus a case ending, serving as the object of bilmek, duymak, söylemek, düşünmek and the like.

b1.name: Wanted actions: -mAsInI istemek, -mAsInA izin vermek
b1.note: When the two subjects differ, the wanted action is nominalised with -mA + possessive + case: Gelmeni istiyorum (I want you to come).
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb in -mA carrying a possessive plus a case ending as the complement of istemek, izin vermek, söylemek and similar verbs.

b1.name: Cause clauses: -DIğI için, -DIğIndAn, -DIğIndAn dolayı
b1.note: The reason clause is nominalised, not introduced by a conjunction: Hasta olduğum için gelmedim.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb in -DIğI (or -(y)AcAğI) with a possessive, followed by için, or ending in -DIğIndAn (+ dolayı).

b1.name: Time clauses: -DIğI zaman, -DIğIndA, -DIğI sırada
b1.note: The same nominalised clause with zaman / -(n)DA gives 'when': Eve geldiğim zaman herkes uyuyordu.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb in -DIğI with a possessive, followed by zaman / sırada, or carrying -(n)DA (geldiğimde).

b1.name: Passive voice -Il- / -In-
b1.note: -ıl/-il after a consonant, -n after a vowel or an l: yazıldı, açıldı, okundu, bulundu. The agent, if named at all, takes tarafından.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb carrying the passive -Il- or -(I)n- before its tense suffix.

b1.name: Causative voice -DIr-, -t-, -Ir-, -Ar-
b1.note: Turkish marks 'have someone do it' on the verb: kestirdim (I had it cut), okuttu, yaptırdı, güldürdü. Which suffix a verb takes has to be learned.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb carrying a causative suffix (-DIr-, -t-, -Ir-, -Ar-) before its tense suffix.

b1.name: Reflexive voice -(I)n-
b1.note: -(ı)n- turns the action back on the subject: yıkanmak (to wash oneself), giyinmek, hazırlanmak.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb with the reflexive -(I)n- (yıkandı, giyindi, hazırlandım).

b1.name: Reciprocal voice -(I)ş-
b1.note: -(ı)ş- means the parties do it to each other: görüşmek, tanışmak, mektuplaşmak, bakışmak.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb with the reciprocal -(I)ş- (görüştük, tanıştılar, mektuplaştık).

b1.name: Concession: -mAsInA rağmen, -A rağmen, -sA bile
b1.note: Turkish builds 'although' out of a nominalised clause plus rağmen / karşın, or out of the conditional plus bile / de: Yağmur yağmasına rağmen çıktık; Yorgun olsam bile geleceğim.
b1.test: The sentence contains -mAsInA / -DIğInA followed by rağmen or karşın, or a conditional verb followed by bile or dA.

b1.name: Preference: -mAktAnsA … -mAyI tercih etmek
b1.note: States a choice between two actions: Otobüse binmektense yürümeyi tercih ederim.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb in -mAktAnsA (or -mAk yerine) set against a second nominalised verb.

b1.name: Past necessity -mAlIydI
b1.note: -malıydı / -meliydi says what should have been done: Dün bana haber vermeliydin.
b1.test: The sentence contains a verb in -mAlI followed by -(y)DI plus a person ending.

b1.name: Postpositions and the case they govern
b1.note: Postpositions follow their noun and each fixes a case: -A göre / karşı / doğru / rağmen, -DAn dolayı / başka / beri / önce, and için / gibi / kadar / ile, which take the genitive on pronouns: benim için, benimle, benim gibi.
b1.example: Benim için bir şey yapabilir misin?
b1.test: The sentence contains a postposition (için, gibi, kadar, göre, doğru, karşı, rağmen, dolayı, başka, beri, ile) with its noun or pronoun in the case that postposition requires.

b2.name: The full compound-tense system (hikâye, rivayet, şart on every mood)
b2.note: Every tense and mood can carry -(y)DI, -(y)mIş or -(y)sA, including the moods: gelmeliydi, gelseydi, gelmeliymiş, gelecekmişse. B2 completes the grid begun at B1.
b2.test: The sentence contains a mood suffix (-mAlI, -sA, -(y)A) carrying a further -(y)DI, -(y)mIş or -(y)sA.

b2.name: -mIş as an adjective (resultant state)
b2.note: -mIş before a noun describes the state left by an action: pişmiş yemek, kırılmış cam, yorulmuş insanlar.
b2.test: The sentence contains a verb in -mIş standing before a noun as its modifier, not as a finite predicate.

b2.name: Lexicalised participles -(A/I)r and -mAz
b2.note: The aorist and negative aorist form fixed modifiers and compounds: çıkmaz sokak, akar su, inanılmaz, okuryazar, tükenmez kalem.
b2.test: The sentence contains a verb in the aorist or in -mAz used as a modifier or as part of a fixed compound.

b2.name: -(y)AsI participle
b2.note: A wish or desirability participle, mostly in fixed expressions: görülesi yerler, öpülesi eller, kahrolası. Rare, and worth teaching mainly for recognition.
b2.test: The sentence contains a verb in -(y)AsI used as a modifier.

b2.name: -cAsInA and -mIş gibi (as if)
b2.note: Expresses pretence or comparison of manner: Her şeyi biliyormuş gibi konuştu; Beni tanımıyormuşçasına baktı.
b2.test: The sentence contains a verb in -cAsInA, or a verb in -mIş / -Iyormuş followed by gibi.

b2.name: -mAksIzIn (without, formal)
b2.note: The written-register counterpart of -mAdAn: Hiç durmaksızın çalıştı.
b2.test: The sentence contains a verb ending in -maksızın/-meksizin.

b2.name: -DIğI sürece, -DIğI boyunca, -DIğI süresince (as long as)
b2.note: Sets the span over which the main clause holds: Sen yanımda olduğun sürece mutluyum.
b2.test: The sentence contains a verb in -DIğI with a possessive, followed by sürece, süresince or boyunca.

b2.name: -DIğI takdirde and -mAsI durumunda (in the event that)
b2.note: The formal conditional of contracts and notices: Yağmur yağdığı takdirde maç ertelenir.
b2.test: The sentence contains -DIğI takdirde or -mAsI durumunda / hâlinde.

b2.name: -(y)AcAğI zaman / sırada (just as, when about to)
b2.note: Places the main event at the moment before another: Tam çıkacağı sırada telefon çaldı.
b2.test: The sentence contains a verb in -(y)AcAğI with a possessive, followed by zaman or sırada.

b2.name: Reported speech across all sentence types
b2.note: B2 extends B1's -DIğInI to questions and commands: yes/no questions become -Ip -mAdIğInI sormak, and orders become -mAsInI söylemek. Tense inside the clause is kept, not shifted as in English.
b2.test: The sentence reports a question with -Ip -mA…-DIğInI / -(y)AcAğInI + sormak, or an order with -mAsInI + söylemek / istemek.

b2.name: Descriptive compound verbs -(y)Iver-, -(y)Adur-, -(y)Agel-, -(y)Ayaz-
b2.note: A second verb adds aspect to the first: açıver (just open it, quickly), bakadur (keep looking), süregelmek, düşeyazdı (nearly fell).
b2.test: The sentence contains a verb in -(y)A/-(y)I followed by a bound ver-, dur-, gel-, kal- or yaz- (açıverdi, bakakaldı, süregelmiş).

b2.name: Compound verbs with etmek, olmak, yapmak and fused forms
b2.note: Noun + helper verb makes most of the abstract vocabulary: yardım etmek, mutlu olmak, telefon etmek. Some compounds are fused and govern a case: vazgeçmek (-DAn), başvurmak (-A).
b2.test: The sentence contains a compound verb of the noun + etmek/olmak/yapmak type, or a fused compound such as vazgeçmek, başvurmak, hoşlanmak.

b2.name: Stacking voice suffixes
b2.note: Causative, reciprocal and passive can be piled on one stem in a fixed order: yaptırıldı (was had made), görüştürüldü, öldürüldü. Reading these apart is the B2 skill.
b2.test: The sentence contains a verb carrying two or more voice suffixes in sequence (e.g. -DIr- + -Il-, -(I)ş- + -DIr-).

b2.name: -mAktA(dIr), the formal present
b2.note: The register of reports, news and academic prose: Çalışmalar devam etmektedir. It states an ongoing fact without the immediacy of -Iyor.
b2.test: The sentence contains a verb in -makta/-mekte, usually with -dIr.

b2.name: -DIr as assumption and as formality
b2.note: Beyond the copula, -dır marks a confident guess (Şu an evdedir — he must be home now) and the impersonal register of notices (Sigara içmek yasaktır).
b2.test: The sentence's predicate ends in -dır/-dir/-dur/-dür/-tır… expressing an assumption or a formal statement, not a plain identification.

b2.name: değil after a participle: gidecek değilim, gelmiş değil
b2.note: değil can negate a verb form as well, denying an intention or a claim: Ben oraya gidecek değilim (I have no intention of going).
b2.test: The sentence contains a verb in -(y)AcAk or -mIş followed by değil plus a person ending.

b2.name: -mIş ol- and -(y)AcAk ol- (perfect and prospective)
b2.note: ol- carries the tense while the first verb carries the aspect: bitirmiş olacağım (I will have finished), gidecek oldum (I was about to go).
b2.test: The sentence contains a verb in -mIş, -(y)AcAk or -Iyor followed by a finite form of olmak.

b2.name: -(y)Abil in the compound tenses
b2.note: The ability suffix takes further tense and mood: gelebilirdim (I could have come), yapabilseydim, gidebilmiş.
b2.test: The sentence contains -(y)Abil- followed by a compound tense or mood ending (-Irdı, -sAydI, -mIş, -mAlI).

b2.name: Word formation: derivational suffixes
b2.note: -lIk, -CI, -CIk, -sEl from nouns; -Im, -gI, -gIç, -(y)IcI from verbs. Recognising them is what lets a B2 reader guess an unknown word: öğretmenlik, gözlükçü, toplumsal, bilgi, alıcı.
b2.test: The sentence contains a word visibly derived by a productive suffix such as -lIk, -CI, -CIk, -sEl, -gI, -Im or -(y)IcI.

b2.name: Consonant doubling and vowel dropping in borrowed stems
b2.note: Arabic-origin stems restore a doubled consonant or a long vowel before a vowel: af → affetmek, his → hissetmek, hak → hakkı; and some native stems drop their middle vowel: burun → burnu, şehir → şehri.
b2.example: Beni affettiği için şehrin en mutlu insanıyım.
b2.test: The sentence contains a stem showing a doubled consonant (affetti, hissetti, hakkında) or a dropped middle vowel (burnu, şehri, oğlu) before a suffix.

b2.name: Contrast and comment connectors: oysa(ki), hâlbuki, meğer(se), mademki, ne var ki
b2.note: The written-language connectors of argument: oysaki and hâlbuki mark a contrast with what was just said, meğerse a discovery, mademki a premise, ne var ki a drawback.
b2.example: Erken çıktım, oysaki yine geç kaldım.
b2.test: The sentence contains one of oysa(ki), hâlbuki, meğer(se), mademki, ne var ki, üstelik, bilakis, yeter ki joining two clauses.

c1.name: The conjunction ki and its fixed patterns
c1.note: Borrowed from Persian, ki opens a clause after the main one, against the normal verb-final order: O kadar yorgundum ki hemen uyudum. Fixed pairs: demek ki, yeter ki, öyle ki, o kadar … ki. It is not the same as the suffix -ki.
c1.example: O kadar yorgundum ki hemen uyudum.
c1.test: The sentence contains ki as a separate word joining two clauses (not the suffix -ki in evdeki / benimki).

c1.name: -mAklA and -mAklA beraber / kalmayıp
c1.note: -makla states the means or the act itself: Gelmekle iyi ettin. -mAklA beraber concedes, -mAklA kalmayıp adds: Gelmekle kalmayıp yardım da etti.
c1.test: The sentence contains a verb in -makla/-mekle, alone or followed by beraber, birlikte or kalmayıp.

c1.name: Formal conditions: -mAsI şartıyla / koşuluyla, -DIğI takdirde
c1.note: The register of agreements and rules: Erken gelmen şartıyla seni bekleriz.
c1.test: The sentence contains -mAsI şartıyla / koşuluyla, or another formal conditional phrase built on a nominalised verb.

c1.name: Impersonal academic register: -Il-mAktAdIr, -DIğI görülmektedir
c1.note: Written Turkish reports findings without an agent, stacking the passive on -mAktAdIr: Bu konu ayrıntılı olarak incelenmektedir; Sonuçların tutarlı olduğu görülmektedir.
c1.test: The sentence's predicate combines a passive suffix with -mAktA(dIr), or is a -DIğI clause followed by görülmektedir / anlaşılmaktadır / belirtilmektedir.

c1.name: Experiential nominalisations: -mIşlIğI var / yok, -DIğI olur
c1.note: Says whether something has ever happened or happens from time to time: Hiç uçağa binmişliğim yok; Bazen geç kaldığı olur.
c1.test: The sentence contains -mIşlIk with a possessive plus var/yok/ol-, or -DIğI followed by olur/oluyor in this sense.

c1.name: Sentence elements and the pre-verbal focus position
c1.note: Turkish word order is free, and the slot immediately before the verb carries the focus: Bu kitabı ben aldım answers who, Ben bu kitabı aldım answers what. Moving a constituent changes the emphasis, not the grammar.
c1.test: The sentence departs from the neutral subject-object-verb order so that a marked constituent stands immediately before the verb.

c1.name: Inverted sentences (devrik cümle)
c1.note: In speech, poetry and headlines the verb leaves the final position: Bilmiyorum ben bunu; Geldi sonunda o gün.
c1.test: The finite verb is not the last word of the sentence.

c1.name: Compound sentence types: sıralı, bağlı, birleşik
c1.note: Two or more clauses joined by a comma (sıralı), by a conjunction (bağlı), or embedded one in the other (birleşik). C1 is where learners build and punctuate these deliberately.
c1.example: Yağmur yağıyordu, biz de evde kaldık.
c1.test: The sentence contains two finite clauses joined by a comma or by a conjunction, or a subordinate clause embedded in a main clause.

c1.name: Tense shift for effect (anlam/zaman kayması)
c1.note: A tense used outside its own time: the present continuous for a fixed future (Yarın gidiyorum), the aorist for a promise, the present for a past narrative.
c1.test: The sentence uses a tense suffix for a time other than its basic one, with a time adverb making the mismatch visible (yarın + -Iyor, and so on).

c1.name: Formal and academic set phrases
c1.note: The connectives of formal prose: söz konusu, bu bağlamda, buna ek olarak, dolayısıyla, itibaren, -DIğI göz önünde bulundurulduğunda.
c1.example: Söz konusu çalışma, konuyu ayrıntılı biçimde ele almaktadır.
c1.test: The sentence contains a set formal phrase such as söz konusu, bu bağlamda, buna ek olarak, dolayısıyla, bu doğrultuda.

c1.name: Idioms and figurative meaning (deyimler, mecaz)
c1.note: Fixed expressions whose meaning is not the sum of their words: işin altından kalkmak, göz atmak, kafa yormak, eli sıkı.
c1.test: The sentence contains a recognised Turkish idiom used with its figurative meaning.

c1.name: Fine-grained adverbs: henüz, daha, artık, zaten, şimdilik, ancak
c1.note: These separate meanings English blurs: artık (from now on, no longer), zaten (anyway, in any case), henüz / daha (not yet), ancak (only, but).
c1.example: Artık burada çalışmıyorum, zaten hiç sevmiyordum.
c1.test: The sentence contains at least one of artık, zaten, henüz, daha (in the 'yet' sense), şimdilik, ancak, yalnızca used with its distinct meaning.

c1.name: Secondary functions of the case suffixes
c1.note: Beyond place and goal: price and manner in the dative (ucuza aldık, boşuna), time span in the locative (bir saatte), cause in the ablative (korkudan, sevinçten).
c1.test: The sentence contains -A, -DA or -DAn used for price, manner, duration or cause rather than for place, goal or source.

c1.name: Voice and subject agreement across coordinated clauses
c1.note: A C1 writer keeps the voice consistent when clauses are joined, and keeps subject and verb agreeing: Kapılar kilitlendi ve ışıklar söndürüldü, not a mix of active and passive with one subject.
c1.test: The sentence has two or more coordinated clauses whose verbs agree in voice (both active or both passive) and whose subjects agree with their verbs.

c1.name: Advanced postpositions and connectives: dışında, yanı sıra, itibaren, nazaran, karşın
c1.note: The written-register set: bunun yanı sıra (besides this), -DAn itibaren (as of), -A nazaran (compared with), -A karşın (despite), -In dışında (apart from).
c1.example: Bunun yanı sıra yeni bir öneri sundu.
c1.test: The sentence contains one of dışında, yanı sıra, itibaren, nazaran, karşın, doğrultusunda with its noun in the case it requires.

c1.name: mI in emphatic repetition and rhetorical questions
c1.note: The question particle also intensifies (Ev güzel mi güzel — the house is beautiful indeed) and forms rhetorical or insinuating questions (Gelmez mi hiç?).
c1.test: The sentence repeats a word around mI for emphasis, or uses mI in a question that is not asking for an answer.

c1.name: Adjectives used as nouns with a possessive: mavisini, küçüğü
c1.note: An adjective plus a possessive (and case) stands for the noun: Mavisini beğendim; Büyüğünü aldık.
c1.test: The sentence contains an adjective carrying a possessive suffix (plus a case ending) and standing in place of a noun.
